Set a new alarm: The user asks to create or schedule a new alarm, possibly with a time, date or recurrence, e.g. 'wake me up at 6 tomorrow'.
Check existing alarms: The user asks for information about alarms already set: which alarms exist, when one goes off, or how long until it rings.
Delete an alarm: The user asks to cancel, delete or remove one or more existing alarms so they no longer exist; merely turning an alarm off is silencing it.
Change an alarm: The user asks to modify an existing alarm, such as moving it to another time, adding minutes to it, changing its days or making it repeat.
Silence or turn off an alarm: The user asks to turn off, stop, disable, dismiss or skip an alarm, ringing or upcoming, without deleting it and without snoozing it.
Snooze an alarm: The user asks to snooze an alarm, postponing its ring for a short period so it sounds again later.
Send a message: The user asks to write and send a text, voice or video message to one or more people or groups.
Read or check messages: The user asks to read, show or find messages, or asks whether a message was sent or received.
React to a message: The user asks to put a reaction on an existing message, such as a like, heart, laugh or sad face.
Ignore a message: The user asks to ignore a message they received: not reply to it, not have it read out, or disregard the notification.
Cancel a message: The user asks to cancel, stop or quit a message they are sending or composing, so it is not sent.
Play music: The user asks to start playing music: a song, artist, album, genre, playlist or radio station.
Skip to the next track: The user asks to skip the current song and move forward to the next or a later track.
Replay the current track: The user asks to play this current song, album or playlist again from the beginning; asking for the last or previous song again is going back instead.
Go back to the previous track: The user asks to go back to or hear again the last or previous song, album or station, the one before the current one, e.g. 'repeat the last song'.
Pause the music: The user asks to pause playback temporarily so it can be resumed from the same point.
Stop the music: The user asks to stop or turn off the music or station entirely, ending playback.
Remove or block music: The user asks to remove a song, artist or genre from a playlist or from what gets played, e.g. 'don't play this song again' or 'no rap music'.
Shuffle music: The user asks to play songs, an album, artist or playlist in random shuffled order.
Create a playlist: The user asks to make a new playlist, optionally naming it or saying which songs to put in it.
Add to a playlist: The user asks to add a song, artist or album to an existing playlist.
Loop the music: The user asks to put a song, album or playlist on continuous repeat, or to keep playing it, so it loops rather than playing once more.
Like the music: The user approves of a song, artist or channel so it is marked as liked: a thumbs up, favouriting it, or saving it to their library.
Dislike the music: The user rates a song or artist negatively, such as a thumbs down or saying they do not like it, so it is marked as disliked.
Traffic information: The user asks about traffic conditions, such as congestion, jams, accidents, delays or closures on a road or route.
Travel time: The user asks how long a trip will take, i.e. the expected duration of travel between places.
Directions or route: The user asks for directions or the best or fastest route to get somewhere, possibly by a travel mode.
Distance: The user asks how far it is between two places, in miles, kilometres or similar.
Arrival time: The user asks when they will arrive, or whether leaving at some time gets them there by a deadline.
Departure time: The user asks when they need to leave in order to arrive somewhere at a given time.
Road conditions: The user asks about the physical state of roads, e.g. flooding, ice, snow, construction damage or obstructions.
Change or reroute directions: The user asks to change the current route, e.g. for a detour, alternate route or avoiding something ahead.
Find a place: The user asks to find or locate a place, such as the nearest gas station, store or stop, or their own current location, not features along a route.
Route features: The user asks what is on or along a route or road, such as tolls, detours, rail crossings, bike lanes, gas stations or attractions along the way.
Create a reminder: The user asks to set a new reminder for themselves or others about a task or event, often with a time.
Delete a reminder: The user asks to cancel, delete or remove one or more existing reminders.
Look up reminders: The user asks to see or check which reminders exist, for a time period, person or topic.
Change a reminder's time: The user asks to move an existing reminder to a different date or time.
Ask when a reminder is: The user asks for the date or time at which a particular existing reminder is set.
Change a reminder in general: The user asks to edit an existing reminder in a way that is not only a new time or only a new task, e.g. its recurrence, who it is for, or unspecified changes.
Change a reminder's task: The user asks to change what an existing reminder is about, replacing or adding the item, task or activity it names, e.g. adding an item to a list reminder.
Ask where a reminder is: The user asks for the place or address attached to a reminder or its event.
Count reminders: The user asks how many reminders they have, overall or for a period or topic.
Get help with reminders: The user asks how to use the reminder feature or for guidance on doing something with reminders.
Start a new timer: The user asks to set or start a new countdown timer for some duration, often for a named activity.
Check a timer: The user asks about an existing timer, such as how much time is left or how long it has run.
Pause a timer: The user asks to pause, hold, stop or turn off a running timer so it stops counting, without cancelling, ending or deleting it.
Add time to a timer: The user asks to extend a running timer by adding extra minutes or seconds to it.
Cancel a timer: The user asks to cancel, end, clear, delete or remove a timer entirely; merely stopping a running timer is pausing it.
Resume a timer: The user asks to continue a paused timer from where it stopped.
Restart a timer: The user asks to restart or reset a timer so it counts again from its beginning or from a new starting value.
Change a timer's settings: The user asks to change or edit an existing timer, usually setting it to a different total duration or start, rather than adding or removing time.
Take time off a timer: The user asks to shorten a running timer by removing some minutes or seconds from it.
Weather conditions or forecast: The user asks about current or forecast weather, such as temperature, rain, snow, wind or humidity somewhere.
Sunset time: The user asks when the sun will set, or about sunset, on some day or at some place.
Sunrise time: The user asks when the sun will rise, or about sunrise, on some day or at some place.
